searchText: I am not sure if I am missing something or not but why is EIP-1559 a new transaction type from EIP-2930? Because it introduces two new properties and removes one. So then could I just use the transaction type 1 if I didn't want my gas being burned? Is that how it works or am I missing something. A better way to ask is there any advantage to use one or the other? All transactions get "upgraded" to 1559 transactions during the block production and validation process. It is strictly worse to use 2930 or legacy transactions compared to 1559 transactions. The automatic upgrade results in the worst possible 1559 transaction for you essentially. I see, does that mean that 2930 transactions are already obsolete? They will continue to work, but I wouldn't recommend using them if you have the option to use 1559. Same with legacy transactions.
